directions.opportunity: The applied-entry set is entity-qualified but the diagnostic-side match is entity-blind: applied keys are built as entity + NUL + identity (change-compiler.ts:122) while the filter tests key.endsWith(NUL + item.identity) (change-compiler.ts:126). In a cross-type same-identity delta — exactly the model family this change legalizes — an already-applied entry of one entity type suppresses ADDED_IDENTITY_EXISTS / MODIFIED_IDENTITY_MISSING / REMOVED_IDENTITY_MISSING diagnostics produced for a different entity type.
directions.impact: Closes the last identity-only matcher so the archive validation gate (src/core/archive.ts:278, compileChange with allowAlreadyApplied) and pending-sync assessment (src/core/archive.ts:245 via getPendingChangeSync) can no longer treat a delta as valid because a cross-type counterpart entry was already applied; also replaces the per-diagnostic [...applied] array spread (O(diagnostics x entries)) with an O(1) Set lookup.

directions.recommendation: Match diagnostics to the applied set by exact key `${item.entity}\u0000${item.identity}` whenever item.entity is set; keep the existing endsWith scan only as the fallback for entity-less diagnostics.
directions.keyDesign: suppressApplied keeps building the entity-qualified applied Set; the filter becomes: item.entity defined ? !applied.has(`${item.entity}\u0000${item.identity}`) : ![...applied].some(key => key.endsWith(`\u0000${item.identity ?? ''}`)). Key construction is identical to the applied-set writer, so same-entity suppression is bit-for-bit unchanged and only cross-type mismatches stop matching.
preservationConstraints: Suppression for diagnostics whose (entity, identity) exactly matches an applied entry MUST remain identical, including the three filtered codes, the allowAlreadyApplied option, and the empty-applied early return
The strict compile path without allowAlreadyApplied (used by prepareChangeSync) MUST be untouched

Diagnostic codes, messages, ordering, and entity values MUST NOT change; only cross-type false-suppression cases stop being suppressed, which is the intended fix and must be locked by a new regression test
The endsWith fallback for entity-less diagnostics MUST remain available even though no current emitter of the three codes reaches it
implementationOutline: In suppressApplied, replace the unconditional suffix scan with an exact applied.has lookup when item.entity is defined, falling back to the existing endsWith scan otherwise

directions.priorityReason: Ranks first because it hardens the entity-scoping mechanism this change just shipped at near-zero cost (a keyed Set match), guards a real gate (archive validation), and its same-entity behavior is provably unchanged; the next direction is a larger-surface pure performance win with no defect component.

directions.opportunity: Bulk validation re-reads and re-parses the entire formal Semantic Model once per item: every queued change calls compileChange(process.cwd(), id) without options.base and every queued contract calls validateElementContract, which starts with readFormalSemanticModel(process.cwd()); on this repo (176 files, 1.2MB, 155 contract-bearing element units) one `xirang validate --all/--contracts` run performs roughly 155 + (active changes) full parses of the same tree, which does not change during the run.
directions.impact: Drops bulk validation from O(items x full model parse) to one shared parse — a user-visible wall-clock reduction at this repo's own scale — with no API or output change, because CompileChangeOptions.base already exists as the sharing seam.
evidence: src/commands/validate.ts:395 — validateElementContract begins with `await readFormalSemanticModel(process.cwd())` and is queued once per contract id in runBulkValidation
src/commands/validate.ts (validateChangeWithPreview) — compileChange is called without options.base, queued once per change id
src/core/change-compiler.ts:150 — `const base = options.base ?? await readFormalSemanticModel(projectRoot)`: the seam already exists

src/core/model/delta.ts (cloneState/ensureOwnedElement/ownedElements) — applySemanticDelta clones before mutating, and Validator.validateElementContract (src/core/validation/validator.ts:121) only reads, so one ParsedModel can be shared across the concurrency-6 task pool
test/commands/validate.test.ts — existing bulk-validate coverage anchors behavior preservation
directions.recommendation: Resolve readFormalSemanticModel(process.cwd()) once per bulk run before queue construction and pass it to every queued item: options.base for compileChange and a new optional base?: ParsedModel parameter for validateElementContract; leave single-item paths unchanged.
directions.keyDesign: runBulkValidation creates one shared Promise<ParsedModel> for the run; each change task awaits it and calls compileChange(root, id, { base: shared }), each contract task calls validateElementContract(validator, id, shared). If the shared parse rejects, the same failure is fed to every queued task so per-item BulkItemResult error rows are preserved instead of the run crashing before any result.
preservationConstraints: Per-item reports, issue messages, exit codes, JSON shape, result ordering, and summary totals MUST be identical to per-item parsing
A shared-parse failure MUST still produce one failed row per queued item with the same message shape as today's per-task catch, not an unhandled runBulkValidation rejection
The shared ParsedModel MUST remain read-only in every consumer (applySemanticDelta already clones before mutation; the contract validator only reads)
Single-item validate paths (--change, direct contract validation) MUST keep their current self-contained parse
All items in one run MUST compile against the same snapshot; model files do not change during a run, so results are observationally identical
implementationOutline: Add optional base?: ParsedModel to validateElementContract and use it in place of readFormalSemanticModel when provided

In runBulkValidation, create the shared formal-model promise once when the scope has items, await-with-catch inside each task, pass options.base to compileChange and the parsed model to validateElementContract
Spot-check `xirang validate --contracts --json` totals before/after to confirm identical output
validation: Existing test/commands/validate.test.ts bulk cases prove identical reports and exit codes
A before/after timing of `xirang validate --contracts` demonstrates the parse-count drop (155+ parses to 1)
pnpm build and pnpm lint prove type and style gates hold
directions.priorityReason: Ranks second: statically provable repeated-I/O elimination with existing seams and verified read-only consumers, but pure performance on an already-correct path, so it yields to direction 1's defect-class hardening; the analogous double-read between change-sync.ts (getPendingChangeSync/prepareChangeSync) and writeMinimal's internal readModelTree stays deferred because change-sync.ts and parser.ts are outside base scope and only writeMinimal's optional-parameter half would be actionable without a caller change.
